scopeDecisions.decision: Observation is through the REST surfaces (Identity Toolkit, Secure Token, Admin v2). SDK paths only where a row needs them, within AUTH-CONFIG-SDK K1 (Admin SDK for Node, Web SDK in Node).

O1: the external IdP boundary is observed with IdPs the lane controls on fireemu-oracle-idp. The OIDC id_token flow uses an issuer whose discovery document and public JWKS are deployed to the sandbox's Firebase Hosting, with ID tokens signed locally. SAML uses a locally made certificate and locally signed responses (SP-initiated). Private keys, API keys and project numbers never enter git; provider configurations and the Hosting content are deleted after each campaign. Owner ledger 2026-09-27 (AUTH-FEDERATION, O1 to O6).

O2: the google.com sign-in success path (a sandbox service account's generateIdToken) is out of scope; google.com is observed through its configuration and its refusals only. Owner ledger 2026-09-27 (AUTH-FEDERATION, O1 to O6).

O3: the OIDC code flow (returnRefreshToken, oauthRefreshToken, oauthAuthorizationCode) is deferred to a separate budgeted stage; it needs a token endpoint service on the sandbox. Owner ledger 2026-09-27 (AUTH-FEDERATION, O1 to O6).

Third-party providers (facebook.com, apple.com, twitter.com, github.com, microsoft.com, yahoo.com, playgames.google.com) are out of scope for their success paths, which need real accounts; their configuration and refusals are observed. The browser behaviour of /__/auth/handler is out of scope. Owner ledger 2026-09-27 (AUTH-FEDERATION, O1 to O6).

O4: the strict profile verifies signed assertions of configured providers: OIDC ID tokens with keys given at startup (the auth.customTokenSigners pattern: a JWKS per issuer) and SAML responses with the provider's idpCertificates, with no network fetch from the issuer; strict refuses the unsigned fixture assertions. The emulator profile keeps the official emulator's fixture IdP and adds no refusal. Owner ledger 2026-09-27 (AUTH-FEDERATION, O1 to O6).

O5: verifying signed SAML XML needs XML canonicalization and XMLDSig; whether that is feasible on the sandbox is checked first, and adding a crate for it is a new owner decision at that point. Owner ledger 2026-09-27 (AUTH-FEDERATION, O1 to O6).

O6: tenant IdP sign-in, tenant provider configuration and blocking functions on IdP sign-in belong to AUTH-TENANT-BLOCKING (as A8, C4, K10); MFA after an IdP sign-in belongs to AUTH-MFA; Admin linkProviderUserInfo and deleteProvider are verified in AUTH-ACCOUNT. Owner ledger 2026-09-27 (AUTH-FEDERATION, O1 to O6).
Budget: US$10 per observation task, as for the other sandbox lanes. Owner ledger 2026-09-27 (AUTH-FEDERATION, O1 to O6).
Moved here: client signInWithIdp sign-in and linking (AUTH-ACCOUNT A4) and the IdP session claims (AUTH-CREDENTIAL C7).

The spConfig.spCertificates production issues and answers for a SAML provider whose requests are signed is a known difference: fireemu does not generate it (it needs an X.509 certificate dependency). Implementing it is a later issue. Owner ledger 2026-09-29 (AUTH-FEDERATION F11).

conditions.note: signInWithIdp and createAuthUri for an unconfigured, a disabled and an enabled provider. Strict answers production's configuration messages (record-oidc 39209e): OPERATION_NOT_ALLOWED : The identity provider configuration is not found. for a provider without a configuration (also one named in another case, and a built-in provider without one), and ... is disabled. for a disabled one; the same for SAML providers.

A controlled OIDC IdP (O1): ID tokens signed with the run's key and published through the sandbox's Hosting; the signature, iss, aud (clientId), exp, iat, nbf, alg and kid matrix and malformed tokens (record-oidc 39209e), and stale iat, azp and several audiences (record-saml 7789f0). Each refusal carries production's message. An issuer without configured keys answers production's INVALID_IDP_RESPONSE : Error connecting to the given credential's issuer. (step unpublished-issuer): fireemu reads auth.idpSigners where production fetches the issuer's keys (O4).
conditions.limits: The exact width of production's staleness window is unobserved: rows at iat 300 to 7200 seconds back with a future exp were accepted, and the refusal was observed for exp and a future iat.

conditions.note: The nonce: absent and present, matching and not (the SHA-256 of the raw nonce in postBody).
The same ID token used twice.

A controlled SAML IdP (O1): SP-initiated responses signed with the run's certificate (record-saml 7789f0). The signature in each position (saml-smoke efe0ef and record-saml 7789f0); a tampered signature and an unsigned response refused with production's two messages (record-followup b72af6); a response without NameID refused. Strict refuses, with production's messages, a status other than success, a Destination other than the callback URL, an assertion Issuer other than the IdP entity ID, audience restrictions without the SP entity ID, Conditions not yet valid or expired, an expired bearer confirmation, and an InResponseTo missing from or other than the request. The Recipient and an expired IdP certificate are accepted, as production accepted them.
conditions.limits: The signature refusals are recorded twice in record-followup b72af6 (saml/signature): a tampered signature is refused with INVALID_IDP_RESPONSE : Failed to verify the signature in SAMLResponse, and a response with no signature at all with INVALID_IDP_RESPONSE : Missing signature in Assertion and Response enclosing it (if present). The InResponseTo check applies only to a sign-in naming a sessionId that fireemu's createAuthUri issued within the last hour; a sign-in without one is unobserved and not refused. Unobserved: which refusal wins when several conditions fail, and a time that does not parse (not checked). The verifier does not implement inclusive canonicalization, other transforms, EncryptedAssertion, or responses past its size and namespace limits; those are refused with INVALID_IDP_RESPONSE. A resumed pendingToken continuation checks the conditions again against the live configuration, all but InResponseTo (closure review SF5): a strict-profile safety choice, since production's continuation is unobserved. SHA-1 signatures and digests are accepted. The blocking-function commit re-verifies the signature and the enabled state but not the conditions, so a slow beforeSignIn can commit after NotOnOrAfter or after the entity IDs change. A response without NotOnOrAfter has no time bound, and a sign-in without a sessionId can replay the same response.

conditions.note: Providers this parent does not sign in with (F3, F5): malformed and synthetic credentials for google.com and the other built-in providers. Without a configuration, production's OPERATION_NOT_ALLOWED : The identity provider configuration is not found. (record-oidc 39209e); with google.com configured, its INVALID_IDP_RESPONSE : Unable to parse Google id_token: <token> for a garbage ID token (record-saml 7789f0). A genuine built-in credential cannot be observed (F3), so accepting one stays a known divergence: fireemu fetches no Google or Facebook key.
